pll1d9c1-d1e3477.summary: Announces the transition to the distinction of persons.

pll1d9c1-d1e3480.summary: Restates from the De fide ad Petrum that the three are naturally one God, none being the other; in the one essence the Father is not aliud from the Son and Spirit, though personally alius.
claims: The three persons are naturally one God.
The persons are personally other, but not other in essence.

pl-l1d9c1.summary: Turns to the distinction of persons and restates the rule of faith from the De fide ad Petrum: Father, Son, and Spirit are naturally one God, yet none is the other. In the one essence they are not another thing (aliud) but another person (alius).
claims: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are naturally one God.
None of the three persons is the other.
In the one essence the persons are other (alius) personally but not another thing (aliud).
